To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the proprioceptive hand localization can be shifted by visuo-motor synchronization, even when the sense of body ownership is not affected.
visuo-movement congruence, but not visuo-movement incongruence, can induce proprioceptive drift of one's hand toward a fake robot hand, but not a sense of ownership for this fake hand.
1) visuo-motor synchronization induces proprioceptive drift towards the fake body part (the robot hand) and 2) visuo-motors synchronization does not affect ownership.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether visuo-motor coordination can be sufficient to induce embodiment effects.
the question of whether the experience of body representation can be modulated by purely visuo-motor stimulation, without the need of visuo-sensory input.
the mechanisms underlying the representation of the body and its border in space, as well as the processes that allow the integration of the body and external objects.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the robot hand illusion is an example of the rubber hand illusion, but with a visuo-motor component.

proprioceptive drift can be induced by visuo-motor synchronous stimulation, even in the absence of visuo-tacile stimulation, but that visuo-motory synchrony is not sufficient to induce a sense of body ownership.

visuo-movement congruence can drive the proprioceptive drift of the hand towards the robot hand, while visuo-movement asynchrony does not, even when the sense of ownership for one's own hand is maintained.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the sense of ownership of one's own hand is not necessarily related to the sense of localization of one's hand, and that the latter is more likely to depend on visuo-motor than visuo-sensory congruency.
proprioceptive drift can be induced by visuo-motor rather than by visuo-tactil congruency.
visuo-muscular congruency is sufficient to induce proprioceptive drift, while visuo-motor synchronization is required for the induction of the rubber hand illusion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
visuo-motors synchrony can drive proprioceptive localization of our own body parts even when somatosensation is kept constant and ownership is maintained.
proprioceptive drift can be modulated by visuo-motor rather than visuo-tactil congruency.
the proprioceptive system is sensitive to visuo-motor information, and that the sense of body ownership is not necessarily required for the proprioceptive system to be modulated by external objects.
